issues.description: The solution declares Genre.name with private visibility but Client.swift accesses genre.name from a different file. In Swift, private restricts access to the declaring file, so the access in Client will not compile. The problem statement expects a plain String property for Genre.name and the template leaves Genre unimplemented, so making the property private in the solution is a visibility mismatch that breaks the intended usage and will prevent successful compilation.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the visibility of the Genre.name property so it is accessible from Client.swift. For example, declare it as a regular stored property (remove the private modifier): `let name: String`. Alternatively, if intentional file scoping is desired, move Client's printing logic into the same file or provide a public accessor for the name (e.g. a public computed property). Removing `private` to make it internal (module-visible) is the simplest and matches the problem specification.
